videoTitle: The Golden Toad: 1,500 to Zero in Two Years
description:
More than fifteen hundred golden toads gathered to breed in a Costa Rican cloud forest in nineteen eighty-seven. Two years later, only one was seen.

This documentary follows the golden toad through its tiny mountain home, its extraordinary colours, its brief breeding season, the failed pools of nineteen eighty-seven, the last confirmed sighting, and the difficult scientific search for a cause.

intro.narration: In nineteen eighty-seven, a hidden cloud forest seemed to turn gold. More than fifteen hundred tiny toads gathered beside rain-filled pools. scenes.title: A World Only Kilometres Wide
scenes.subtitle: High in Costa Rica's cloud forest
scenes.narration: The golden toad lived in one tiny part of Costa Rica. Its known home lay high in the cloud forest near Monteverde. Mist kept the leaves wet, while moss covered roots and fallen wood. The entire known range measured only a few square kilometres. A change in one small forest could touch the whole species.

scenes.title: Fifteen Hundred, Then Failure
scenes.subtitle: The pools dried in nineteen eighty-seven
scenes.narration: In the spring of nineteen eighty-seven, researchers counted more than fifteen hundred adult golden toads at five pools. It looked like abundance. But the rain stopped, and the shallow water shrank. Thousands of eggs and tadpoles were lost as the pools dried. At most, only twenty-nine young toads completed the change to life on land.

scenes.title: The Collapse
scenes.subtitle: Almost nothing returned
scenes.narration: Researchers came back when the next breeding season began. The forest was still there, and the pools filled again. The golden crowds did not return. Across repeated searches from nineteen eighty-eight through nineteen ninety, only eleven toads were found. A population once counted by the thousand had collapsed almost overnight.

scenes.title: The Last Golden Toad
scenes.subtitle: One male in nineteen eighty-nine
scenes.narration: In May of nineteen eighty-nine, a single male appeared. He was small, bright orange, and alone. No one knew that this ordinary field record would become the final one. Later searches covered the known range, but no golden toad answered the rain. That male remains the last confirmed member of his species.

scenes.title: A Forest Without Its Toad
scenes.subtitle: Protection could not explain the silence
scenes.narration: This was not a simple story of a forest being cut down. The golden toad lived inside protected cloud forest, and much of that habitat remained. Yet a reserve could not control the weather, stop a hidden disease, or protect a species beyond its boundary. The empty pools became a scientific mystery. The answer had to reach beyond habitat loss alone.

scenes.title: Drought, Disease, and Uncertainty
scenes.subtitle: No single cause tells the whole story
scenes.narration: The final collapse followed an exceptionally dry period linked to a powerful El Niño event. Dry pools explain the failed breeding season, but not every missing adult. Scientists also point to chytrid, a deadly fungus that swept through many American amphibians. Climate can change the conditions in which disease spreads and animals survive. The exact balance is still debated, so one cause should not carry the whole blame.

scenes.title: A Warning From the Clouds
scenes.subtitle: Small ranges leave little room
scenes.narration: The golden toad became an early symbol of the worldwide amphibian crisis. Its tiny range made every bad season more dangerous. Its disappearance also showed that a protected map is only the beginning of protection. Conservation must watch disease, climate, water, and sudden changes before numbers crash. The warning from Monteverde still belongs to living species everywhere.

outro.title: Protection Must See the Invisible
outro.subtitle: A standing forest can still lose a species
outro.hookText: Its forest survived. The toad did not.
outro.narration: The golden toad left no final photograph of a rescue and no captive group to return. It left an empty pool and a lesson about threats we cannot always see.
